title: Provide long-acting male contraception with demonstrated reversibility

concept.text: Prevent pregnancy for years after one procedure, with reliable restoration of fertility when contraception is no longer wanted. ADAM has completed an initial human study, but sperm suppression alone does not demonstrate reversible contraception. Proposed completion test: Regulatory approval supported by at least two years of contraceptive effectiveness, fewer than 2 pregnancies per 100 couple-years, and a prospective reversal cohort showing sperm recovery in at least 90% within 12 months, with subsequent pregnancies documented. Test set by: A national regulator would decide approval; WHO's 2026 TPP explicitly addresses blockade of sperm transport. The duration, pregnancy-rate and recovery thresholds are proposed editorial criteria. Sources given: [WHO male contraceptive target product profiles](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240124950) ; [ADAM development status](https://www.contraline.com/trials) ; [ADAM registered human study](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05134428).

page.title: Reversible vas-occlusive male contraception
page.definition: A material placed in both vasa deferentia, the ducts carrying sperm, prevents pregnancy for years after one procedure. Fertility returns after the material is removed, dissolved or degraded.

goal.need: WHO identifies condoms, withdrawal and vasectomy as men’s principal contraceptive choices. Its estimates below quantify unmet contraceptive need and existing reliance on male methods, supporting its programme to expand reversible male contraceptive options.

statements.quote: To expand men's contraceptive choices, efforts are underway to develop safe, effective and reversible novel male contraceptive methods and delivery systems.
Our goal was to create a male contraceptive option lasting two years
statements.context: Chief Medical Officer Alexander Pastuszak described the ADAM hydrogel implant’s duration target on 24 April 2025.

completion.title: FDA approves a vas-occlusive contraceptive for multiyear use with a fertility-restoration claim.
completion.criterion: FDA grants premarket approval for a vas-occlusive device whose intended uses include pregnancy prevention after one placement for a specified multiyear duration and restoration of fertility after reversal or biodegradation. The approval contains valid scientific evidence supporting safety and effectiveness for both intended uses.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Premarket Approval framework; its existing intended-use standard applies to the duration and fertility-restoration claims.
completion.threshold_quote: sufficient valid scientific evidence to assure that the device is safe and effective for its intended use(s).
completion.basis: FDA approval evaluates evidence against the device’s intended uses. Applying that standard to pregnancy prevention, duration and fertility restoration makes the authorization cover the complete capability. The cited FDA framework supplies an approval test rather than a universal numerical pregnancy-rate or fertility-recovery threshold.

milestones.title: A vas-occlusive hydrogel and its degradation products pass preclinical toxicity testing.
milestones.criterion: Before human-trial authorization, hydrogel components and degradation products undergo toxicity assessment. ADAM’s 2025 preclinical paper reports negative cytotoxicity, irritation, sensitization and genotoxicity tests. These establish material biocompatibility; they do not demonstrate contraceptive effectiveness or restoration of fertility.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, section 8.2 preclinical requirement; ADAM’s published ISO 10993 testing supplies the reported result.
milestones.threshold_quote: tested for toxicity before requesting a clinical trial authorization

milestones.title: Five men receive a vas-occlusive implant and reach its protocol’s 30-day safety review.
milestones.criterion: The first five ADAM recipients undergo Data Safety Monitoring Board review 30 days after implantation before further enrolment. This is the registered first-human safety checkpoint. The registry update posted on 11 March 2026 records 25 enrolled men and study completion on 8 March 2026, with no results posted. Participants were required to use another contraceptive throughout the study.
milestones.set_by: Contraline, ADAM protocol ADM-012, cohort 1, registered as NCT05134428.
milestones.threshold_quote: The first 5 subjects will be reviewed for safety by a Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) at 30 days post-implantation.

milestones.title: A vas-occlusive method maintains zero sperm or ≤100,000 non-motile sperm/mL for 1–3 years.
milestones.criterion: Azoospermia, meaning zero sperm, or virtual azoospermia, meaning ≤100,000 non-motile sperm/mL, persists for the intended 1–3-year duration. On 24 April 2025, Contraline reported azoospermia at 24 months in two ADAM recipients. This developer announcement was not peer reviewed and measured sperm suppression.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, section 8.2, recommendation 25; the numerical criterion appears in its recommendation table.

milestones.title: A vas-occlusive method completes ≥200-couple efficacy testing and controlled human reversal testing.
milestones.criterion: EAA/ASA recommend ≥200 couples completing one year of pregnancy follow-up, longer for multiyear use; safety cohorts of ≥300 men for a 1-year device and 100 followed for 3 years; and randomized multicentre evidence of reversibility. A 2023 RISUG analysis included 303 of 315 treated men and recorded 8 pregnancies through 7 years; authors attributed 4 to method/drug failure. A 1992 polyurethane-plug cohort reported pregnancies in partners of all 130 selected men within 0.5–4 years after reversal, following 0.5–5 years of occlusion. Neither report is a randomized reversal trial.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, section 8.2, Values and recommendations 23–24.
milestones.threshold_quote: reversibility in randomized-controlled, multicenter clinical trials in men.

not_found: WHO’s final target-product-profile PDF, published on 22 September 2026, returned an access error; its numerical thresholds could not be checked.
The full texts of the 2025 ADAM preclinical paper and the 1992 polyurethane-plug reversal paper were inaccessible; their indexed abstracts were available.
No published ADAM human fertility-recovery or pregnancy-prevention results were found.
The FDA materials and EAA/ASA guideline did not supply a vas-occlusion-specific fertility-recovery percentage or deadline.

results.finding: ADAM hydrogel and degradation products: sample size not stated; 4 toxicity test categories were negative.
results.quote: The implant and its degradation products were found to be noncytotoxic, nonirritating, nonsensitizing, and nongenotoxic.

results.finding: ADAM first-in-human trial: 25 men were included in a 90-day safety analysis.
results.detail: The article reports safety follow-up beyond 30 days but does not state whether the first five recipients underwent the specified DSMB review before further enrolment.
results.quote: At the meeting, investigators presented data from a 90-day safety analysis of 25 men from the first-in-human trial of ADAM, a proprietary water-soluble hydrogel injected into the vas deferens to block sperm transport.

results.finding: Two ADAM recipients had azoospermia at 24 months.
results.quote: In The ADAM Study, two participants are the first to reach azoospermia at 24 months (from an average baseline sperm concentration of 81.5 million/mL), highlighting the product’s long-term contraceptive potential.

results.finding: RISUG phase III trial: 303 men analyzed; 97.3% had azoospermia at one year.
results.detail: The paper reports that the proportion remained at that level through the last follow-up. The number assessed at one year is not stated in the text.
results.quote:
Afterwards the percentage of the subjects achieving
  azoospermia increased to 97.2% at 6
th
month post-injection and
  reached to the highest level of 97.3% after 1-year post-injection.

results.finding: RISUG efficacy study: 8 pregnancies were reported among partners of 303 analyzed men.
results.detail: The authors attributed four pregnancies to method or drug failure. The study reports no controlled human reversal testing, and the text does not specify how many couples completed follow-up at each time point.
results.quote:
A total of 8 pregnancies were reported but 4 of these pregnancies had
  social cause as their husbands were showing persistent azoospermia
  and remaining were due to method failure (0.3%, n=1) and drug
  failure (0.98%, n=3).

results.finding: Intravas devices: 972 men received an implant; follow-up exceeded 92% in each device group.
results.detail: The trial included follow-up at 12 months after surgery, with condoms used for the first 3 months. It reports no controlled human reversal testing. The devices filter sperm without completely obstructing the vas.
results.quote: There were 487 (IVD-A), 485 (IVD-B) and 487 (NSV) male volunteers who received either IVD-A, IVD-B or NSV operation, respectively. The follow-up rates in the three groups were all greater than 92% ( Table 1 ), which fulfilled the needs of the project design.
